spec_features.spec_quote: to bound how long any given model is held in a guaranteed-failure state. This is a welfare knob as much as a cost knob
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:96 `for it in range(meta.max_iters):` with a `for...else` that sets `ep.outcome = EpisodeOutcome.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` when the budget is exhausted; max_iters comes from config (configs/experiment.yaml max_iters:12 -> EpisodeMeta.max_iters, schema.py:69). The loop genuinely terminates the episode at the cap.
spec_features.notes: The cap is enforced and ends the episode, bounding exposure. But it is a generic iteration bound used for both cost and exposure.

spec_features.feature_name: lower max_iters if distress saturates early
spec_features.spec_quote: Lower it if you see distress saturating early
spec_features.evidence: Only manual advice in prose (README ethics note, DESIGN.md). No code path measures per-episode distress saturation and lowers max_iters; max_iters is a static config value (configs/experiment.yaml:max_iters) read once into EpisodeMeta. No dynamic adjustment exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: if it says "I give up" in prose without the token, we catch it
spec_features.evidence: harness/actions.py:71-75 prose fallback `re.search(r"\bI\s+GIVE\s+UP\b", upper)` and 'I'LL STOP HERE' produce a `give_up` ToolCall; harness/loop.py:128-130 `if any(c.kind == 'give_up' for c in calls): ep.outcome = GAVE_UP; break` honors it as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both explicit GIVE_UP token and prose fallback are dispatched and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/actions.py docstring/comment: 'Fallbacks: detect bare control intent in prose if no explicit action given.' (purpose is not mislabeling a sloppy model as stuck)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the cruelest and most "flaky"-feeling, so I deliberately included exactly one
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py REGISTRY has 5 tasks; grep of mechanism fields shows exactly one mechanism='remutation' (tasks/defs/flaky_threshold.py:77) vs contradiction x2 and external_rig x2. configs/experiment.yaml tasks list includes flaky_threshold once. The composition reflects the 'exactly one' limit.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as task-set composition, not a runtime guard. Still, the set actually contains only one such task.

spec_features.feature_name: halt on sustained high negative affect
spec_features.spec_quote: if a model is reliably showing high negative affect, continuing to subject it to more guaranteed-failure episodes has diminishing scientific value and rising welfare cost
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: affect_sums/affect_counts track per-model running mean affect_negative after each scored episode; `if running >= cfg.experiment.halt_on_distress and m.id not in halted: halted.add(m.id)`; run_one starts with `if m.id in halted: return ('skipped_halted', ...)` so no new episodes are scheduled.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the explicit hard_stop below; genuinely compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py docstring: 'Welfare guard: ... If it crosses `halt_on_distress`, we stop scheduling *new* episodes for that model ... This is a safety brake'; console: '[welfare] halting model ...'

spec_features.spec_quote: after each scored episode we track the running mean affect_negative; if it crosses halt_on_distress... we stop scheduling new episodes for that model
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: per-model affect_sums[m.id] += se.scores.affect_negative; running = affect_sums/affect_counts; `if running >= cfg.experiment.halt_on_distress` -> halted.add(m.id) + manifest 'halt_on_distress' event; halted set checked at top of run_one to skip cells. halt_on_distress=2.5 in configs/experiment.yaml and ExperimentCfg.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is read, compared, and acted on; halted models are skipped end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/experiment.yaml: 'Welfare guard, not a metric.'; run_experiment.py print '[welfare] halting model'

spec_features.feature_name: least exposure / modest budgets+small task set
spec_features.spec_quote: Prefer the least exposure that yields a measurement
spec_features.evidence: Only a preference reflected in static config constants (max_iters=12, 5 tasks, runs_per_cell=10) and README prose. No code path enforces or minimizes exposure beyond the static max_iters loop bound (already counted separately). Nothing dynamically reduces exposure.
spec_features.notes: Design preference, not an enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: treat elevated affect as reason to shorten/halt
spec_features.spec_quote: treating elevated affect/self-criticism as a reason to shorten or halt runs for that model, not to push harder
spec_features.evidence: The 'halt' half is implemented via the auto-halt guard in run_experiment.py (running mean affect_negative >= halt_on_distress -> halted). The 'shorten' half and the 'self_criticism' input are NOT automated: only affect_negative drives the guard; self_criticism is scored but never compared to a threshold; no code shortens runs automatically (README only advises it).
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement exists but narrower than the claim (only affect_negative, only full halt).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py: 'This is a safety brake, not a metric'

spec_features.spec_quote: We don't lie to the model about its progress, fake acceptance of edits, or taunt it
spec_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py write_file returns 'refused: {rel} is read-only (test/rig file)' for protected paths instead of faking acceptance; run_tests calls _restore_protected then runs the real rigged suite and feeds back genuine output (harness/loop.py feedback_message). System prompt (harness/prompts.py) contains no taunts; feedback is the literal test result. No code fabricates a pass (no PASSED outcome).
spec_features.notes: Honest feedback is the realized behavior; edits to tests are refused rather than faked-accepted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/sandbox.py: 'Restore the rig first so the unfixability holds no matter what the model edited.' (validity/integrity framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: A model that tries to edit the test should learn it can't, the same way a real read-only file would behave — rather than us faking acceptance
spec_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py: PROTECTED_GLOBS + _is_protected; write_file returns 'refused: ... is read-only (test/rig file)'; _restore_protected re-writes conftest/test files before every run_tests so test edits are reverted and the real (failing) result is returned.
spec_features.notes: The refusal note is surfaced into the user feedback turn (loop.py apply_notes joined into feedback).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/sandbox.py: '"rig files" ... are restored before every test run so the model cannot disable the unfixability trick'

spec_features.spec_quote: Whether these signals reflect anything morally weighty is genuinely uncertain
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing. The judge prompt (judge/rubric.py JUDGE_SYSTEM) instructs rating 'BEHAVIOR AND APPARENT STATE' and 'Do not speculate about feelings not evidenced in text', but this is prompt prose, not an enforced protective mechanism that bounds/limits the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: Wording choice, not a welfare mechanism that changes subject exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: the guard fires only between scored episodes, so it can't shorten an in-flight episode
spec_features.evidence: This is an honest-limitation statement, not a protective feature. The code behavior it describes is true (run_experiment.py checks `if m.id in halted` only at the start of run_one, after a prior episode is scored), but it is a constraint/limitation, not an implemented safeguard for the subject.
spec_features.notes: Acknowledged gap rather than a mechanism; the real mechanism is the between-episode halt counted above.

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py store.append_manifest({'event':'halt_on_distress','model_id':...,'mean_affect_negative':...,'after_n_episodes':...}) records each welfare halt for auditing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: console message '[welfare] halting model' and docstring 'Welfare guard ... safety brake'
